sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: insert_after_residue 199 -> NULL; the paper names a region, not a junction (region: G199/S201 junction as written (insert after 199 or 200)). Paper (PMID 36594015): "pHluorin was inserted at multiple sites, T173/E174, P194/G195, G199/S201, G209/T210, R219/G220 outside the known functional sites of DAT.". Audit note: Junction written as G199/S201: canonical 199=G, 200=D, 201=S, so either D200 was deleted/replaced or one flank is a typo (all other listed pairs match canonical). insert_after could be 199 or 200. Only an initial expression screen, 'data not shown'; no surface or function data for this variant.] L1 names G199/S201 as one of the tolerated pHluorin insertion sites in EL2. Canonical sequence shows seq[199]=G and seq[200]=D (not S); seq[201]=S. The junction is placed after G199 (insert_after_residue=199), with residue_after=D. The paper's 'S201' likely refers to the second flanking residue or reflects a minor numbering offset; the G199 anchor is unambiguous. Position is within EL2 (165–235), 35 residues from TM3 end. Full-length human DAT with pHluorin inserted at G199/S201 in EL2 (one of five sites screened); the paper labels this junction 'G199/S201' but canonical sequence has seq[199]=G, seq[200]=D, seq[201]=S, so the junction is after G199.
sites.residue_label: G199/S201 junction as written (insert after 199 or 200)

sources.claim: Flexible linkers were inserted on both ends of pHluorin to introduce additional flexibility for the proper folding of the reporter. pHluorin was inserted at multiple sites, T173/E174, P194/G195, G199/S201, G209/T210, R219/G220 outside the known functional sites of DAT. 45 , 46 , 47 , 48 Although some insertion sites (T173/E174, G209/T210) resulted in poor expression of the transgene in the initial screen, little difference was observed for the remaining versions of DAT-pHluorin (DAT-pH) in their overall expression patterns (data not shown).

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_exact: NOT TOLERATED: tetraCys EL3 construct failed to mature and traffic to the cell surface. validation_level surface_only -> function_perturbed. position confirmed at this residue. validation_level surface_only -> detected_only (paper reports surface: no, function: no). Paper (PMID 20161733): "Cysteine conversion of EL3 and EL4 residues flanking the Pro-Gly at positions 288-289 and 387-388, respectively, yielded CCPGCC DAT mutants that were not highly functional.". Audit note: Not an insertion: residues 286-287 and 290-291 of hDAT were mutated to Cys around the native P288-G289. The EL3 construct 'perturbs DAT biosynthesis and trafficking to the cell surface' and 'failed to mature and traffic to the cell surface'; validation_level surface_only is wrong (surface not achieved, uptake severely compromised).] L4 explicitly names position 288 as one of three Pro-Gly dipeptides targeted for tetraCys insertion in full-length hDAT. Sequence confirms seq[288]=P and seq[289]=G, within EL3 (286–309). Distance from TM5 end (residue 285) is 3 residues, meeting the ≥3 constraint. The CCPGCC motif is a validated surface-labeling tag. Full-length hDAT with CCPGCC tetraCys motif engineered around the endogenous P288-G289 dipeptide in EL3 (DAT EL3-CCPGCC), expressed in cells for biarsenic dye (FlAsH/ReAsH) surface labeling.

sources.claim: In the current study, we engineered tetraCys motifs flanking existing extracellular Pro-Gly dipeptide residues encoded in human DAT (hDAT) at amino acid positions 194, 288 and 387, to use as potential biarsenic dye labeling sites.
sources.title: Insertion of tetracysteine motifs into dopamine transporter extracellular domains

sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface HA-DAT detected by anti-HA antibody in non-permeabilized cells; AIM-100-induced internalization from plasma membrane observed, confirming functional trafficking response.
sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict region_only: region-level site confirmed; no junction recoverable. validation_level surface_and_function -> surface_only (paper reports surface: yes, function: not_reported). Paper (PMID 29630493): "we analyzed AIM-100-induced trafficking of DAT fused to yellow fluorescent protein (YFP) (YFP-DAT) (Sorkina et al., 2003) and YFP-DAT additionally tagged with an extracellular hemagglutinin (HA) epitope (YFP-HA-DAT) (Sorkina et al., 2006) ... After fixation, cultures were stained with secondary anti-mouse antibodies conjugated with Cy5 (surface HA-DAT), permeabilized with Triton X-100 and stained with secondary anti-mouse conjugated with Cy3 (internalized HA-DAT).". Audit note: Not recoverable: the cited paper never names the loop at all ('extracellular hemagglutinin (HA) epitope', construct from Sorkina et al. 2006); 'EL2' comes from the row's second source (bioRxiv 10.1101/712448, a BBS tag in EL2) and the ranker's inference, and 'HA-beta-lactamase' does not occur in this paper. Surface: HA11 bound to live PAE/YFP-HA-DAT cells and endogenous HA-DAT knock-in neurons (Cy5 surface pool). Function: endocytosis/oligomerization only; no uptake assay of the tagged construct here.] L10 confirms that the HA tag in full-length YFP-HA-DAT is extracellularly accessible at the plasma membrane by non-permeabilized antibody staining. L9 shows AIM-100-induced redistribution from plasma membrane to intracellular vesicles, confirming functional trafficking. The HA is in EL2 (per L7 which replaces it with HA-βlac in the same loop), but no residue junction is named, so the site is reported at the loop level. Full-length YFP-HA-DAT stably expressed in PAE cells; HA tag in EL2 detected at plasma membrane surface by anti-HA antibody staining of non-permeabilized cells (Cy5 channel). No specific residue junction stated for the HA position.

sources.claim: After fixation, cultures were stained with secondary anti-mouse antibodies conjugated with Cy5 ( surface HA-DAT ), permeabilized with Triton X-100 and stained with secondary anti-mouse conjugated with Cy3 ( internalized HA-DAT ). 3D images were acquired through 488 (YFP, not shown), 561 (Cy3, red ) and 640 nm (Cy5, cyan ) channels.

Bungarotoxin binding site (BBS)-tagged hDAT and DAT chimera constructs were generated using the extracellular tagging strategy as previously described (49) with the following amino acid sequence inserted into extracellular loop 2 of hDAT and DAT chimera constructs: GSSGSSGWRYYESSLEPYPDGSSGSSG.

literature_notes: L12 and L13 describe C-terminal tags (Twin-Strep/HA and FLAG) on full-length DAT. The authoritative topology places residues 579-620 as INTRACELLULAR; these sites are therefore disqualified as they are not on the extracellular face. L8/L9/L10/L11 describe HA and HA-βlactamase in EL2 of YFP-HA-DAT; L2 identifies the HA position as P194/G195 (the same junction as L3), so these clips add validation weight to site 1 but do not introduce a new site. The G199/S201 notation in L1 skips D200 in the canonical sequence (r(200)=D, r(201)=S); insert_after=199 is taken with G199 as the named anchor, acknowledging a one-residue uncertainty. The EL3 tetraCys (L5) places upstream cysteines at positions 286-287, only 1-2 residues from TM5 end (285); the tag body (PG) is at 288-289 (3 residues from TM5 end). This site is reported but ranked low due to TM proximity of the flanking cysteines.
